package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update mechanism was compromised to deliver malicious code (Sunburst backdoor) to customers. Attackers inserted a backdoor into the legitimate update, enabling remote access and control over customer systems, including government and private sector networks. This supply chain attack allowed widespread espionage and data exfiltration.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update installation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a backdoor that beacons to attacker-controlled servers, receives commands, and executes them on the victim system. The code is obfuscated and designed to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes outbound connections to remote servers not associated with SolarWinds, receives and executes remote commands, and is obfuscated to avoid detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update code should not include hidden remote access or command execution logic, nor should it communicate with unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may beacon to known, trusted servers for updates or telemetry, but not in a hidden or obfuscated manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code in a business logic DLL
Outbound network connections to non-SolarWinds domains
Dynamic command execution from remote source
Execution at service start or update install

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises SolarWinds build environment and injects malicious code into Orion update DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to customers via legitimate update mechanism.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised update, loading the malicious DLL into Orion services.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on customer systems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code beacons to attacker-controlled servers, receives commands, and executes them (e.g., lateral movement, data exfiltration).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent, covert access to victim networks.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion services to non-SolarWinds domains
Obfuscated or anomalous code in business logic DLLs
DLLs or binaries with unexpected export functions or network activity
Unusual process behaviors at service start or update install
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with hash not matching official release
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in Orion installation directory
network_indicators: Connections to known Sunburst C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Beaconing patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion service processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to domains not owned by SolarWinds. Check file hashes of Orion DLLs against official releases to detect tampering. Analyze business logic DLLs for obfuscated code or unexpected export functions. Use network monitoring to identify beaconing behavior and block known C2 domains associated with Sunburst.
